study: Gated OS scheduler CPU allocation under fixed runnable opportunities
status: portable prospective protocol; current hardware may be unsupported
workload: Pure-Python deterministic dense matrix multiplication and independent matrix-vector consistency check, single Python thread; no BLAS calls
primary_endpoint: Measured worker user plus system CPU seconds by fixed log-size class, including partial jobs and loop overhead
secondary_endpoint: Completed jobs multiplied by independent mean CPU cost per job, compared with actual CPU charged to completed jobs
opportunity_measure: Predeclared number of continuously runnable equal-priority single-thread workers in each fixed log-size class
allocation_hypothesis: Equal CPU time per runnable process under existing contention and inherited ordinary scheduling; class share proportional to runnable worker count
competing_hypotheses: equal job service per runnable process
equal CPU allocation per active class
hardware_gate: Every condition needs more workers than a verified inherited CPU bound no greater than two; quota-only bounds additionally need period <= trial/10 and zero burst; no priority, affinity, or cgroup settings are changed
inference_scope: OS policy and workload allocation under declared opportunity counts; no power-law exponent fit, no autonomous selection principle for Nature
